key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders priced in potential rate hikes following Fed Chair Warsh's warning; global rate uncertainty weighs on Australian equities
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict, pressuring BHP, RIO, and FMG valuations
Construction sector under stress: Bathla's collapse signals broader industry fragility, with housing construction expected to follow falling prices
EV adoption in Australia has crossed a tipping point (BYD commentary), reshaping consumer and energy sector dynamics
Victoria's soaring debt triggers ratings agency warnings, raising sovereign credit concerns
Qantas operational incident (engine fire, flight diversion) raises safety and reputational risk for QAN.AX
Gold miners (Aurum) report high-grade discoveries; small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche) lead ASX runners
ASIC launches whistleblower review at major accounting firms, adding regulatory overhang to financials
CBA and Westpac found to exploit legal loopholes charging loyal customers more, inviting political and regulatory scrutiny
El Nino-driven cyclone triplets pose near-term insurance and infrastructure risk across Queensland

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; gold and critical-minerals small caps outperforming. Aurum adds high-grade ounces; Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche lead ASX runners.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore price softness. Gold (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) and critical minerals (VNR.AX, PCH.AX) offer relative strength. War-driven demand diversification may support LNG and coal names short-term.

sectors.trend: CBA and Westpac face political backlash over customer pricing loopholes; ASIC whistleblower review at Big Four accounting firms adds regulatory risk. Victoria debt warnings pressure state-linked credit.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX may face margin pressure from regulatory intervention. Rate hike fears (Warsh) support NIMs but cap multiples. Defensive positioning warranted.

sectors.trend: EV sales have overtaken petrol cars in Australia; BYD declares tipping point reached. Hidden costs (charging infrastructure, battery replacement) emerging. VW cutting 50,000 jobs globally signals auto sector distress.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WTW.AX face demand shift. EV charging and battery names gain. Oil & gas (WDS.AX, WLE.AX) face structural headwinds but near-term support from geopolitical risk premium.

sectors.trend: Australians report feeling poorer; consumer confidence soft. Cigarette tax debate adds political noise. Qantas operational issues dent travel confidence.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBT.AX, LSG.AX under pressure. QAN.AX faces reputational risk from engine incident. Defensive consumer staples preferred.

sectors.trend: Housing construction expected to follow falling prices. Bathla collapse signals construction sector fragility. Brisbane waterfront approval lacks affordable housing. El Nino cyclones threaten Qld assets.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and insurance risk. Construction (WBC.AX, CGW.AX) under stress. Property valuations in Qld at risk from cyclone exposure.

sectors.trend: Vietnam dental tourism threatens Australian dental sector. ASIC review of accounting firms impacts financial infrastructure. AI worker shortage drives skilled migration policy.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX relatively insulated. Tech/AI names benefit from migration policy support. Regulatory scrutiny on Big Four (not ASX-listed) indirectly affects audit costs for listed firms.

key_themes: Global rate hike fears (Fed Warsh) pressuring ASX multiples
Iron ore structural shakeout vs geopolitical demand support
Construction sector fragility and housing downturn
El Nino / cyclone risk for Qld assets and insurance
Regulatory scrutiny on banks and accounting firms

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global rate hike / Fed policy shift
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge rate sensitivity via short-duration bonds; favour dividend-paying defensives; monitor RBA response to AUD/USD moves

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price decline / commodity shakeout
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold (GOLD.AX) and critical minerals (VNR.AX)
Avoid high-leverage construction names; favour established builders with strong balance sheets; monitor housing starts data
Maintain 10-15% allocation to gold and energy hedges; monitor AUD/USD for safe-haven flows

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Nino / cyclone damage to Qld assets
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review insurance coverage on Qld REIT and property holdings; monitor SPC forecasts
Monitor state bond spreads; reduce exposure to state-linked infrastructure plays

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical-minerals small caps
opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical risk premium, iron ore weakness, and high-grade discoveries (Aurum) support gold; critical minerals (vanadium, rare earths) benefit from EV transition and supply-chain diversification

opportunities.recommendation: Add defensive dividend payers ahead of rate uncertainty
opportunities.rationale: ASX lower on rate fears; high-yield defensives (energy, staples) offer income and capital preservation
EV sales surpassing petrol cars marks structural shift; charging infrastructure and battery recycling names gain

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / thermal coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Structural shakeout in iron ore; war-driven demand is temporary; China stimulus uncertain
Bathla collapse signals sector fragility; El Nino cyclones threaten Qld assets; housing construction following prices lower
Fed rate hike warning and global uncertainty pressure AUD; RBA may lag, widening yield differentials

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure in the 1-3 month window. Rate hike fears (Warsh), iron ore softness, and construction sector stress cap upside. Geopolitical volatility (US-Iran, Russia) adds risk premium. 'Bull case returns' narrative offers a counter-narrative but is unproven. Expect range-bound trading with downside bias on ^AXJO.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA holds or cuts, iron ore stabilises, and EV transition drives new demand. Construction sector will see further consolidation. Gold and critical minerals remain structurally supported. Consumer weakness may persist, pressuring retail and discretionary names. Victoria debt and NOM policy remain macro overhangs.
